procedure.description: periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal

denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 19371 (periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal) with date of service 2026-03-07. CARC 96: Non-covered charge(s). RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: Complications of cosmetic implants are a listed plan exclusion.

criteria.text: Baker grade III or IV capsular contracture with pain or deformity, or implant rupture confirmed by imaging.
Capsulectomy and implant removal are not covered when the original implants were placed for cosmetic augmentation, regardless of subsequent complication.
Symptoms documented for at least 3 months.

chart.text: From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

36 year old woman here about her implants. Discussed capsulectomy with implant removal and the options for replacement versus leaving them out. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypertension on lisinopril. Allergies: no drug allergies. Quit smoking 5 years ago, no alcohol, works two jobs. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Right breast is hard as a rock, distorted upward, tender to the touch, I would grade it Baker IV. Left is a Baker III, firm but not painful. Implants went in in 2012, cosmetic augmentation, saline, done out of state. No history of breast cancer. The hardening on the right started about 10 months ago and has gotten steadily worse, now hurts to lie on that side.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 199, LDL 156, HDL 46, triglycerides 172. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
MRI breast implants: right implant with a linguine sign consistent with intracapsular rupture, thickened capsule. Left implant intact with a thickened capsule and no rupture.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Back to go over the MRI and the plan. She wants the right one out and both capsules addressed. Vitals today 117 over 76, pulse 84.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Vitamin D came back 24. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Nurse call. Patient had questions about time off work after surgery and whether she needs someone at home the first night. Answered both, she will arrange it.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 18 and 18. No ocular pathology noted.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.2, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Pre-op. Consent signed for bilateral capsulectomy with implant removal, right side en bloc if the capsule allows. Labs fine.

expected.note: Plan exclusion: crit-2 (origin) cannot be met by any chart content.
